findings.severity_note: narrow: it needs two lanes' services appending to the shared admission-verdicts.jsonl inside the read-to-truncate window, the loss is one best-effort verdict line, and no admission decision reads this log, so it does not hold the node; the in-place edit is nonetheless worth keeping, since it does remove the fixed .tmp name collision and the inode orphaning the previous helper caused.
findings.text: the docstring of _record_pass_verdicts asserts a line appended while the pass is trimming is not lost, but trim_service_log (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:610) reads the tail in trim_file_ends (:566, a separate open/read that can read the whole 1 MiB bound) and only afterwards opens the path rb+, writes the tail at offset 0 and truncates. A verdict line appended by another lane's admission service inside that read-to-truncate window is written past the truncate offset and discarded, exactly as the replaced os.replace helper discarded one; the stated reason - that the appender's own descriptor stays valid - does not hold either, because _append_crew_log_line (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:76) opens an O_APPEND descriptor per line and closes it in the same call, so no descriptor outlives a single write.

findings.severity_note: follow-on rather than blocking: reaching it needs the log to be over the 1 MiB bound and an open/read on a file the service owns to fail, and the fleet supervisor's own call site (fleet_supervisor.py:1183) is equally unguarded, so this matches the owner's existing contract rather than establishing a new failure mode.
findings.text: trim_service_log can raise OSError (from the stat/read in fleet_supervisor.py:585-599 and from the open(path, rb+) at :624) and _record_pass_verdicts does not guard the call, so on the head the trim can propagate out of the pass; the replaced _trim_log_to_bound swallowed every OSError and returned, and _append_crew_log_line states the write 'may not fail or stall because its record could not be written'. admit_until_stopped (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1248-1257) catches only KeyboardInterrupt, so such an error ends the admit service instead of costing one log line.

findings.severity_note: the fragment is the evidence a later reader trusts, so the overclaim is worth correcting in the same breath as the docstring; it does not affect the node's measured result.
findings.text: the landing paragraph carries the same unestablished claim into the durable record: 'keeps the inode, so the appender's own descriptor stays valid and a line written while the trim runs is not lost.' It names a concurrency guarantee that this node's gate does not test and that the mechanism does not provide for a write landing between the tail read and the truncate, so the record asserts more than its own measure shows.
